name: Field Sales Copilots
blurb: AI assistants that prepare representatives for each visit.
title: Field Sales Copilots
answer: Drugmakers are building assistants that brief representatives before each visit, drawing on a doctor's specialty, prescribing history and past engagement and suggesting tailored messages. Sanofi chose Snowflake's data cloud and Cortex AI to build such tools.

reading.body:
Field sales copilots prepare pharmaceutical representatives for visits using CRM history, prescribing data, and approved materials, and they do not change what a representative is permitted to say.

The pattern is preparation, not autonomy. A copilot assembles a brief from a doctor's specialty, prescribing history, and past engagement, then suggests messages and materials. The compliance boundary stays where it was: promotional rules apply to what a representative says regardless of how the suggestion was prepared, and suggested messages must draw only from approved materials and be logged like any other promotional interaction.

This matters for AI because it shows where the constraint sits. The hard part is not generating a recommendation, it is connecting CRM, commercial data, and content systems so the recommendation can only draw on material already cleared for use. Sanofi's choice of Snowflake's data cloud and Cortex AI is a data-platform decision as much as a model decision, which is consistent with the governance requirement that every suggestion remain traceable to an approved source.

The data covers one vendor selection and the compliance rules around promotional content. It does not give deployment scale, cost, measured effect on prescribing, or how the tools handle a suggestion that falls outside the label.

explainer:
Before a visit, a representative traditionally reviews call notes, prescribing data and approved materials to decide what to discuss. Copilots automate that preparation, assembling a brief and suggesting topics and materials suited to the doctor's interests and past engagement, and afterwards help log the call.

Building them requires connecting CRM, commercial data and content systems, which is why drugmakers are pairing data platforms with AI services. The compliance requirements are the same as for any promotional activity: suggestions must come from approved materials, recommendations must respect the label, and interactions must be recorded.

What a field copilot does

A field copilot is an assistant for sales and medical representatives that sits inside their CRM and mobile tools. Before a call it summarises the account, recent interactions, approved materials and open questions. During a call it can retrieve approved answers. After the call it drafts the visit note, suggests follow ups and logs the interaction. The aim is to spend less time on administration and more time with clinicians, and to make every representative as prepared as the best one.

Why compliance teams care

Everything a representative says about a medicine is promotional and regulated. A copilot that generates its own answers could make an off label claim or misstate a safety fact. The accepted design limits the copilot to approved content, records what it showed, and routes anything outside approved material to medical information. The visit notes it drafts are also records that can be requested in litigation or inspection, so they must be accurate and reviewed.

What success looks like

The measurable gains reported by vendors and early adopters are time saved on call preparation and note writing, more consistent use of approved content, and faster onboarding of new representatives. The harder question is whether clinicians value the interaction more, and that depends on the representative, not the tool. Programmes that treat the copilot as a preparation and record keeping aid, rather than a script, tend to keep both representatives and compliance teams on side.
